races.name: Coral Goodwood Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Maxi King
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Goodwood form at this sort of trip; Toby Moore (7lb claimer) keeps the weight manageable, but on 41 days off and stepping sharply up in distance, the key question is whether he can control a field of 18 without being overhauled before the straight; Good to Firm is fine for him.
runners_data.comment: Maxi King has been knocking on the door, a second two starts back and a third four starts back highlighting consistent placed efforts, and he has experience of today's going — the concern is that he remains yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Oxford
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking is an obvious draw for a horse with back-to-back wins over 2m on similar ground at Sandown; his last two Goodwood runs were modest, but that was at shorter trips — the step back to this extended distance suits, and the headgear-free profile suggests he races honestly.
runners_data.comment: Duke of Oxford won two of his last five starts and returns on a quick 20-day turnaround in good heart, with experience of today's going working in his favour. Carrying 137 lb is the one ask, but his recent winning form makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Defiantly
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's runner showed real promise when second over 2m4f at Goodwood last time, beaten a neck; the tongue-strap is retained, Dylan Browne McMonagle is a top-class booking, and 45 days off has allowed a breathing issue to settle — the trip and course are clearly in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Defiantly has run over today's trip and going before, and he comes here fresh after 45 days off carrying 133 lb — second last time out is the standout angle. The main risk is he's winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Valiancy
runners_data.note: William Haggas horse with a sparkling record of three wins and two places from eight runs on Good to Firm or faster, and three Goodwood starts all placed; the pacemaker headgear (p) suggests he's known to travel prominently, and James Doyle rides a horse seemingly well placed in the weights at OR 97 over a trip he handles.
runners_data.comment: Valiancy boasts back-to-back wins in his recent form and has experience of today's going, making him a serious threat off 132 lb; the main concern is whether a 45-day absence has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Sundance
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on a horse who has won twice over 2m at Sandown and run respectably over 2m4f at Goodwood; the pacemaker headgear flags a desire to race handy, and Andrew Balding's 8-from-40 recent record indicates stable form — his last run at Goodwood over 2m6f saw him finish eighth, but that was a step too far in trip.
runners_data.comment: Berkshire Sundance won two of his last five starts, with those victories three and four runs back, but eighth last time out suggests he's struggling to recapture that form; he has going experience to call on, though 131 lb is a stiff burden.

runners_data.name: Annabel's Ghost
runners_data.note: French raider from M Seror's stable who gets here fresh (45 days) after a run on Soft at Goodwood last summer that petered out at 5th; Pierre-Charles Boudot's ride is notable, and the one British win came at Sandown at 2m — the trip is fine but the stable's limited British record is a reservation.
runners_data.comment: Annabel's Ghost has experience over today's trip and rates 4 lb above his official mark, but a fifth last time out and a stable firing at just 3% in the last 14 days are real concerns; his sole win comes five starts back, with a third four starts back the only other encouragement in recent runs.

runners_data.name: Alphonse Le Grande
runners_data.note: Veteran seven-year-old who has been plying his trade at 2m+ on Soft and Standard surfaces; the trainer (A J Martin) has a modest 1/6 recent record, and his Goodwood runs (12th, 13th) have been poor — the Good to Firm surface is his biggest question mark.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Alphonse Le Grande at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a rating of 92 suggests some unexploited ability — though recent finishes make it hard to fancy him strongly against a field of 18.

runners_data.name: Believitanducan
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent, winning three of his last five including back-to-back at Goodwood over 2m; William Buick's booking on a horse at OR 87 who has placed over 2m5f at Haydock is significant — Alan King has no runners in the last 14 days which may simply reflect patience, and this is a fair mark.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14th of 18 on our figures, Believitanducan rates an outsider on these terms despite a striking run of three wins in his last four starts; he has experience of today's going, but the ratings gap is hard to overcome.

runners_data.name: Anniversary
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up runner carries a tongue-strap and has placed at 2m+ on Good to Firm previously; Jamie Spencer thrives at Goodwood and knows exactly how to stalk the pace here — the concern is a string of 5s suggesting a horse that finishes well but rarely wins, with OR 86 unlikely to be flattered by the ratings ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; Anniversary has going experience in his favour and returns after 20 days, but the recent record of fifths and a seventh underlines the task he faces here.

runners_data.name: Charging Thunder
runners_data.note: Won the 2m6f Goodwood handicap last year from off the pace, which is the single most relevant piece of form in this field; David Probert comes in on a horse who was busy just 12 days ago and is now OR 86 (down from 103 at his peak) — the distance and course suit perfectly but the very quick turnaround needs monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, though a second three starts back offers some hope, and his trainer is in fine shape at 35% over the past fortnight; he has run over today's going before, but an unplaced effort 12 days ago leaves something to prove.

runners_data.name: Highwind
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' runner carries the pacemaker headgear (p) but is mapped as a hold-up type, suggesting he has been campaigned further back at his best; David Egan rides and the Goodwood form (4th at 2m, 6th at 1m6f) is adequate — the absence of any win from 15 Good to Firm runs is a clear caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Highwind does at least bring going experience to the table and a our rating fractionally above his official mark suggests some residual ability — yet a sixth and eighth punctuate that sequence, making him a hard one to fancy from mid-table.

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's horse is a genuine prominent racer by nature, with five consecutive placed efforts in the last six runs at 2m–2m2f on Standard and Soft; because this field is saturated with prominent types, he is unlikely to claim his natural berth and may be racing out of role — his recent form is solid but the scenario where he thrives depends on getting the position his style demands.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sax Appeal has nonetheless shown consistent placing ability, landing four thirds in recent starts; he has run over today's going before, yet ranked 12 of 18 on our ratings, he faces a stiff ask from 119 lb.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Kings
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's lightly-raced four-year-old has placed at 2m1f on Soft and at shorter on Good to Firm; by nature a front-rank runner, the crowded prominent sector means he faces a scenario where he cannot dictate — 70 days off and Saffie Osborne's inexperience at this level add further unknowns.
runners_data.comment: Consistent runner who has finished second three times in his last five starts, though winless in that spell and a 70-day break needs to be factored in; has experience of today's going and the 87 rating suggests he holds his own in this field.

runners_data.name: St Mawes
runners_data.note: George Scott's four-year-old has form figures of 1-1-3-2 over 2m and arrives just 14 days after a void race; a natural front-runner by temperament, he faces the same redistribution problem as Sax Appeal and Sea Of Kings — his winning form is genuinely good but the inability to find his position over 2m4½f with this many rivals wanting to be prominent is a real risk.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 15 of 18 on our figures, St Mawes faces a stiff ask, and a void run complicates his recent profile; he was a winner four and five starts back, and second two starts back shows some form, while he has experience of today's going and is fit enough at 14 days since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Kentucky River
runners_data.note: Two wins over 2m3f and 2m4f at Goodwood on Good to Firm make this horse's course-and-distance profile arguably the strongest in the field; Jack Nicholls (3lb claimer) rides fresh (58 days off), and the hold-up style means he needs the pace to be honest enough — at OR 81 he is a major player if the race is truly run.
runners_data.comment: Kentucky River arrives 58 days between runs and ranks 17th of 18 on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite winning last time out; he has experience of today's going, but the weight of evidence points elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Aggagio
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up specialist by nature, here mapped to midfield due to the volume of genuine closers in this race; the form from his last six runs (3rd-5th-6th across differing surfaces) shows consistency without a win since 2022 — Molly Gunn's 5lb claim helps but Soft-ground form dominates his record and Good to Firm may stretch him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a third two runs back his best recent effort, Aggagio has run over today's trip and going before but a ranking of 13th of 18 on our figures makes it hard to build a case for him here.

runners_data.name: Gooloogong
runners_data.note: George Baker's six-year-old has winning form at 2m on Standard at Lingfield and runs handy by instinct; the field's prominent-type congestion means he, like several others, is unlikely to secure his natural racing position — Isobelle Chalmers' 7lb claim partially offsets the disadvantage but the last Goodwood run (6th at 2m) on similar ground suggests limited ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive finishes of sixth and fourth in his last two starts make Gooloogong hard to fancy despite a win three starts back, and he ranks 16th of 18 on our figures; today's going holds no fears on past experience, but he has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old ran just 7 days ago and is back quickly on Good to Firm having won over 1m6f at Goodwood earlier in his career; a true prominent racer by style, the overcrowded front-rank dynamic in this field means he faces difficulty getting his position, and Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim is a small offset to what looks like a tough ask from a tactical standpoint.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Trojan Sun arrives unplaced last time out and sixth three starts back, with his sole recent victory coming four starts back; going experience helps, but he faces a stiff ask from this position in the rankings.

races.paceDynamic: Maxi King is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of 18 over 2m4½f on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, and with no genuine rival likely to press him for the lead, he should dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a punishing one — sustainable fractions over this marathon trip that reward those travelling well within themselves in the first half of the race. Several horses tagged as true prominent types — Sax Appeal, Sea Of Kings, St Mawes, Gooloogong, and Trojan Sun — cannot all secure their natural position given the volume of pace in the field, meaning a contested early order is possible as those runners jostle for ground behind Maxi King, but the overall tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. The redistribution of prominent types into midfield means there is genuine traffic risk for hold-up horses trying to thread through a compacted bunch from the rear. This race shape strongly favours genuine prominent racers who can sit second or third behind Maxi King and travel fluently, as the pace will be steady enough that those further back will need to come wide and generate their own momentum in the straight, giving an edge to horses with a proven record of racing handy on quick ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Maxi King Controls, Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Maxi King sets a steady, uncontested lead and the prominent horses directly behind him travel comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Maxi King dictates with cover, and the horses who naturally want to race in the top four — Valiancy, Defiantly, Berkshire Sundance — sweep past him in the Goodwood straight where the track rewards those with a clean passage; the Good to Firm ground suits runners who can quicken off a sound surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Find Late Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the compacted midfield breaks apart turning for home, allowing genuine closers to accelerate through late.
scenarios.body: Charging Thunder, who won over this course and distance, and Anniversary both possess the finishing kick to exploit tired rivals if the pace has been honest enough; the wide Goodwood straight occasionally gives late movers a clear run if the field fans out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the volume of prominent types unable to settle creates a fractious early order and the pace becomes uneven, burning out the front group.
scenarios.body: An uneven tempo followed by a crawl would disadvantage the hold-up horses who need a true run but could hand the race to a horse like Believitanducan, whose recent winning streak shows he handles tactical affairs on similar ground; Sea Of Kings, a natural prominent type forced to wait, may also find a clear passage if the field strings out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Outstays Long Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the race becomes a true test of stamina over the full 2m4½f trip.
scenarios.body: A genuinely taxing gallop would bring Kentucky River — a proven winner at extended distances on this course — into play, as his Goodwood form over 2m3f and 2m4f is clearly superior to his flat-track figures; Annabel's Ghost, though lightly exposed at Goodwood, also has a stamina profile that could emerge if the pace proves relentless.

watchPoints.text: Charging Thunder won the Goodwood 2m6f handicap last year from off the pace and now has course-and-distance form figures that eclipse most in this field — watch for him to be covered up early and delivered wide into the straight by David Probert.

Valiancy's Good to Firm record (3 wins, 6 places from 8 runs) combined with James Doyle and a prominent racing style makes him the horse most likely to ambush Maxi King approaching the two-furlong marker — watch how quickly he moves to cover Maxi King's quarters after the half-mile mark.

The volume of prominent types (Sax Appeal, St Mawes, Sea Of Kings, Gooloogong, Trojan Sun) all forced out of their natural position creates a compressed midfield — watch the early exchanges for bumping and interference between the two-furlong and one-mile marks as these runners fail to find their preferred ground.

Maxi King's claimer Toby Moore will have 18 horses immediately behind him from a wide draw — if Moore goes too steady on a long-striding front-runner, the prominent types behind him will be fighting for space at the first bend and the race could develop a false rhythm that makes pace analysis redundant.

races.name: HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Andab
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien three-year-old fresh from a Goodwood placing (7th/7f last time) who is by nature a pace-prominent racer but with three rivals of similar inclination in this field, he is pushed into a midfield slot he won't naturally seek; headgear (blinkers) suggests he needs to be in the action, which makes the compromised position a meaningful concern.|
runners_data.comment: Andab has been consistently thereabouts, placing second and third in four of his last five starts before a seventh last time out, and he has run over today's trip. The concern is that 41 days off the track may have left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Catullus
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's colt boasts a Goodwood win last time out over 7f, goes on Good To Firm, and is highly track-intelligent, but his natural desire to race up with the pace is curtailed here by Talk Of New York's dominance and a crowded prominent group; OR 107 gives him claims but the positional squeeze tempers confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Returned to winning ways two starts back, but unplaced last time out casts doubt on his consistency; he has run over today's trip and carries 129 lb from stall five, while a speed rating of 94 suggests he may need to find more against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Five Ways
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's runner has been gelded and steps up to a mile having campaigned over 5-7f, with form figures of 4-7504 suggesting inconsistency; he is a prominent-type who will struggle to find his preferred spot and faces the additional challenge of an unproven mile trip on this evidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Five Ways faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 20-day break from stall one, but the modest recent form — two fourths the best of it — makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Saber Strike
runners_data.note: William Haggas's colt has the cleanest recent form in the field (1-163) over this course and trip and is one of the two horses most likely to actually secure a prominent position just off Talk Of New York; his Goodwood record (2W from 4) on similar going is a genuine positive and Marquand suits the track well.|
runners_data.comment: Saber Strike arrives here third last time out, and a winner three starts back, with his official mark of 107 underlining his class; the sixth two starts back is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Shayem
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's charge arrives as the second-highest-rated runner (OR 109) and a genuine Goodwood specialist, winning here over this mile trip last time on identical going; Clifford Lee's hold over the horse is a positive, and he should naturally slot into a prominent position where the race is run from.|
runners_data.comment: Shayem arrives here in fine nick — a winner last time out and second two starts back, with experience over today's trip and a fit 22-day turnaround; the main risk is whether 129 lb blunts his late effort.

runners_data.name: Talk Of New York
runners_data.note: OR 116 top-rated, four wins on the card including at Goodwood, trained by Appleby with Buick aboard — the complete package for a front-running dictation job; holds a hood (headgear) which aids concentration, and 45 days fresh is not unusual for this yard targeting a specific race with a sharp horse.|
runners_data.comment: Talk Of New York has been in fine nick, winning three of his last five starts with a win two starts back, and returns from a 45-day break having run over today's trip before; third last time out shouldn't alarm, and at 129 lb he carries plenty but remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Yazin
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's talented three-year-old (OR 104) carries a tongue-tie and returns after 64 days off; he is a natural pace-prominent type whose redistribution to the rear of the field is forced by circumstance rather than preference, and racing out of role from the back of a compact seven-runner field significantly undermines his chances despite Ryan Moore's booking.|
runners_data.comment: Yazin has won three of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, and has run over today's trip, but that distant eighth last time out is a concern after 64 days off, and our rating ranks him last of the seven runners here.

races.paceDynamic: Talk Of New York is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with William Buick in the saddle, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good To Firm ground at Goodwood. Shayem and Saber Strike are the most natural prominent racers in behind, likely to track the leader closely, while Catullus, Andab, and Five Ways are genuine pace-wanting types who will be forced into a more restrained role than they'd prefer given the volume of prominent runners in this seven-horse field. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Talk Of New York should own the rail and the lead, with Saber Strike and Shayem most likely to actually occupy the second and third slots on the fence, leaving Catullus, Andab, and Five Ways shuffled back against their instincts. With a lone, class-advantaged pacesetter in Talk Of New York (OR 116, highest in the field) controlling tempo on a flat mile in Good To Firm conditions, this race shape strongly favours horses capable of racing prominently or just off the pace and quickening, rather than genuine hold-up runners who will find little cover and face a punishing wide run to reel in a comfortable lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Talk Of New York Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Talk Of New York leads unchallenged at a fair but controlled tempo and quickens away in the straight.
scenarios.body: William Buick allows Talk Of New York to stride into a soft lead, controls the fractions from the front, and the Appleby inmate — highest-rated runner at OR 116 with four wins at Goodwood — simply has too much class and reserves to be caught; horses sitting second and third in a prominent position get the best tow into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Talk Of New York goes too hard early and ties up inside the final furlong, leaving a prominent tracker to swoop.
scenarios.body: Should Buick's pace prove even fractionally ambitious, the prominent trackers sitting second and third — Shayem and Saber Strike — are ideally positioned to capitalise without having to make up ground from deep; Shayem's recent Goodwood form and Good To Firm record (3W from 7 at the track) makes him the chief beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent contingent jostles for position early, creating a muddled tempo that opens a gap for a freshened runner.
scenarios.body: With Catullus, Andab, and Five Ways all wanting to race up with the pace but unable to, scrimmaging in the first half-mile could produce an uneven gallop that briefly compresses the field and benefits a horse with cover; Catullus — winner at Goodwood last time, fresh, and trained by Appleby — is best positioned to exploit any resulting bunching.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely slow early tempo sees the field bunch and Yazin, pushed to the rear against his nature, produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Yazin is a true prominent racer displaced to hold-up by field composition, meaning his finishing kick will be deployed from an unnatural position and he faces a significant style penalty; only if the pace entirely collapses and the field concertinas in the straight does he have any realistic hope of threading through.

watchPoints.text: Talk Of New York's ability to stride into an uncontested lead unchallenged is the single biggest factor shaping this race — watch whether any rival attempts to match strides early and disrupts Buick's control of fractions.

Catullus, Andab, and Five Ways will all be angling for the same prominent ground in the first two furlongs — any crowding or interference in that group could cause checking, shuffling, and positional penalties that distort results.

Yazin's 64-day absence and enforced hold-up role combine to create a significant unknown; Ryan Moore may choose to ignore the redistribution and push forward regardless, which could inject unexpected pace and unsettle the projected race shape.

Good To Firm at Goodwood on the flat mile typically rewards horses with a high cruising speed who can maintain tempo through the final two furlongs rather than those relying on a short, sharp sprint — check Shayem and Saber Strike's finishing splits from recent runs.

Saber Strike's headgear-free profile and straightforward front-tracking style makes him a clean positional reference point — if he gets a clean run tracking Talk Of New York, his two previous Goodwood wins on this going confirm he handles the conditions as well as any rival in the field.

races.name: Coral Golden Mile (Class 2 Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed leader in this field; Tudhope can dictate terms on Good to Firm Goodwood where he has strong course form (sim-going 13/15), though he is technically mapped as prominent and his OR=105 means he carries weight — the gift of an uncontested lead is his greatest asset here.
runners_data.comment: Cerulean Bay has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 110 ranks him second of 22 runners — a strong case for him being the chief danger here. A second four starts back shows he can threaten at this level, though he remains winless in recent starts and the quick five-day turnaround is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Archivist
runners_data.note: 44 days off and a headgear note (h) for Hamad Al Jehani's yard (trainer 0/11 in 14 days, cold); won here at Goodwood over 1m and his sim-going record is solid (9/12), but the layoff and quiet trainer form are meaningful flags.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but unplaced last time out, and 44 days on the sidelines adds a fitness query; has experience of today's distance and going, though carrying 138 lb from stall 20 is no light task.

runners_data.name: Ebt's Guard
runners_data.note: Consistent mid-table finisher at Goodwood who rarely wins (1W from strong sim-going record); Muir & Grassick have 2/12 in 14 days — quietly ticking over — but a form string of 4-0443 suggests he fills places rather than takes them.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ebt's Guard nonetheless brings a consistent profile to the table — third last time out, with experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 110 puts him top of this 22-runner field from stall 3 carrying 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Mister Winston
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding has 8/40 in 14 days and Oisin Murphy's booking is significant; won over this exact course and distance (1/8f/GOO in hist) and carries only 136lbs, with a good sim-going record (12/13) — the combination of jockey, trainer form, and course-distance form makes him highly relevant.
runners_data.comment: Mister Winston has winning form in recent starts — a winner two starts back and a winner four starts back — but came home unplaced last time out after 44 days off, so he returns here on a fitness query; he has experience of today's trip and going, though his 136 lb burden from stall 19 is no help.

runners_data.name: English Oak
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has won twice at Goodwood over 1m (sim-going 13/15); ridden by Faleh Bughanaim for the Jehani yard whose trainer stats are cold — but English Oak's own course-distance form is the strongest in the field among the closers.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to finish second last time out after an unplaced run, and English Oak has experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but 135 lb from stall 22 makes life harder for a horse ranked mid-division.

runners_data.name: Indalo
runners_data.note: Roger Varian in excellent 14-day form (8/21) and won here at Goodwood over 1m last time; headgear (h) and sim-going 8/13 — a genuine prominent horse who should actually secure a good position and arrives in peak condition, making him one of the stronger tactical profiles.
runners_data.comment: Indalo won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but he carries 135 lb from stall 6 and ranks eighth of 22 on our ratings — enough ability to feature, though the weight is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Two Tempting
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old returning after 146 days off — that layoff is the dominant flag; all five recent runs at Staplehurst rather than Goodwood (sim-going only 6/15) and the stamina of the form suggests he prefers patient races, but the fitness question after nearly five months is hard to dismiss.
runners_data.comment: Two Tempting shows consistent placing form — third last time out, and a winner five starts back — but 146 days off the track is a concern, and 133 lb is a stiff enough burden; he has run over today's distance and going, at least.

runners_data.name: Classic
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon has 11/52 in 14 days, middling; won over this exact trip at Goodwood (1/8f/GOO) and sim-going is strong (12/15), but form string of 8-2198 shows inconsistency and his natural prominent style puts him in a crowded space behind the leader.
runners_data.comment: Classic showed a useful turn of form with a win three starts back, but his two most recent efforts — eighth and ninth — make it hard to trust him here, especially shouldering 132 lb from stall 12. He has run over today's trip and going, which at least ticks the experience box.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a deeply disappointing recent run record (8-0080); sim-going only 5/15 at Goodwood on this surface and OR=99 looks ambitious given current trajectory — hard to make a case here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ozat nonetheless has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 106 suggests he retains ability; the concern is a consistent lack of placing, making it hard to fancy him strongly from stall five off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Scoville
runners_data.note: William Haggas has 7/38 in 14 days; Marquand takes the ride on a horse with a perfect sim-going record (6/6) who won over 1m at Goodwood — the form dip (104-87) is notable but the horse clearly handles these conditions, and the Haggas/Marquand combination warrants respect.
runners_data.comment: Scoville showed he knows how to win when landing the spoils five starts back, and experience over today's trip and going underlines his claims — but back-to-back sevenths and eighths in recent starts are the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Blue Brother
runners_data.note: Genuinely prominent in style but the field density pushes him back against his nature in this scenario — Jehani yard cold (0/11), sim-going only 3/10, and recent form a concern (5/60-4); the style displacement makes his chance harder to land.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Blue Brother nevertheless shaped with promise on his most recent outing and a rating of 107 from our assessors suggests he's ahead of his official mark — with today's trip already under his belt, he looks a serious threat, though that 43-day absence is the one question to answer.

runners_data.name: Godwinson
runners_data.note: Jack Channon at 4/19 in 14 days; a form string of 500-00 tells its own story, and his Goodwood sim-going (5/15) is the weakest in the prominent group — hard to recommend on any angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn in stall 14, Godwinson faces an uphill task, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 104 offers a sliver of encouragement; 44 days between runs leaves his sharpness open to question.

runners_data.name: Cosi Bello
runners_data.note: Won at 7f here at Goodwood and placed at the track; Charlie Fellowes has 1/13 in 14 days, and his natural front-running tendency gets squeezed out in this crowded prominent bracket — he would need to find a slot that may simply not exist in a 22-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Cosi Bello won three starts back but has disappointed since, finishing unplaced and then sixth in his last two; he has run over today's distance and going, yet 130 lb from stall nine makes life harder for a gelding who needs to rediscover that earlier spark.

runners_data.name: Mirsky

races.paceDynamic: Cerulean Bay is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-runner field on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Daniel Tudhope can control tempo from the front at a pace entirely of his own choosing — a sustainable, measured gallop that preserves reserves into the straight. Behind him, a glut of natural prominent types — Archivist, Ebt's Guard, Mister Winston, Bunyola Bay, Indalo, and several redistributed horses including Blue Brother, Cosi Bello, Beagle Bay, Tribal Chief, Mirsky, and Walsingham — will contest the positions directly behind, creating scrimmage in the chasing pack but no meaningful pressure on the leader. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can physically secure their natural positions; of those, Archivist, Mister Winston, Bunyola Bay, and Indalo are best-placed to actually slot in behind Cerulean Bay, while the rest are shuffled back against their instincts. This race shape — a single uncontested pace-setter controlling tempo — strongly favours horses that can sit close to the leader in the first three or four, travel within themselves, and produce a controlled, sustained kick in Goodwood's long home straight, rather than deep closers who will be trapped in traffic with no genuine pace injection to surf.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cerulean Bay Controls, Close Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay sets a fair but sustainable tempo and the horses immediately behind travel comfortably within their comfort zone.
scenarios.body: Cerulean Bay rolls along on a true but uncontested gallop, and the horses sitting second to fourth — notably Mister Winston, Indalo, and Bunyola Bay — are perfectly placed to peel off the leader's back entering the straight and sustain their runs all the way to the line; the long Goodwood straight rewards those with a measured gallop behind them rather than a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Crawls, Leader Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay is allowed an even more conservative gallop than expected and the chasing pack fails to organise a challenge until far too late.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied and a field of 22 fractured into traffic jams behind, Cerulean Bay dictates every yard, conserves energy, and simply lengthens away from a field that has been too passive to reel him in; horses like English Oak and Scoville, coming from hold-up positions, simply cannot make up enough ground on a winner who has never been tested.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Rises, Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster applies more early pressure than expected and the tempo quickens sufficiently to set up a strong-finishing late run.
scenarios.body: A busier pace caused by jostling in the prominent pack burns off those who have overcommitted, and hold-up horses such as English Oak, Scoville, and Indalo — who drop in when crowded — find daylight in the straight as the leaders tire; Good to Firm ground suits this type of sustained late finish but the lack of a genuine pace injector limits the probability of this shape truly developing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Wide Runners
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 22 produces significant interference in the straight and horses racing wide or with clear daylight gain a decisive positional edge.
scenarios.body: In a messy, scrimmaging race where inside runners are blocked repeatedly through the final two furlongs, those given a wide berth by their jockeys — such as Beagle Bay or Tribal Chief, who despite being remapped are aggressive enough to push wide early — emerge into clear air while rivals are stopped in traffic; this scenario is inherently low-probability because the uncontested lead means the field rarely bunches tight enough to produce blanket interference.

watchPoints.text: Mister Winston and Indalo — both natural prominent types with genuine Goodwood 1m form who should actually secure the positions directly behind Cerulean Bay; if either leads the chasing pack through the final two furlongs, they are the horses most likely to overwhelm the field.

runners_data.name: Jm Jungle

runners_data.name: Lamborghini Bf
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of three wins from four starts including a recent Goodwood 6f victory, but drops to 5f here for the first time at this track; this Swedish raider's natural desire to race prominently puts it at odds with a field already bursting with speed.|

runners_data.name: Partisan Hero
runners_data.note: Showed good recent Goodwood form with a win and back-to-back thirds, Colin Keane takes over and the horse is in fine shape; though a natural prominent runner, the sheer number of pace types in this field means he is likely to find himself doing more work than ideal to get his position.|

races.paceDynamic: Asfoora is the one confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner sprint and, with Oisin Murphy in the saddle, she will break sharply and attempt to control proceedings from the front on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood — a track that rewards those who race prominently on the straight five-furlong chute. The problem for the field is that this race is saturated with prominent types: American Affair, Jakajaro, Rumstar, Spicy Marg, and Time For Sandals all want to be close to the pace, meaning Asfoora will face genuine early pressure even if she gets first run, and the shape will be contested rather than truly uncontested. Jm Jungle, Brussels, Aspect Island, Argentine Tango, Dickensian, Partisan Hero, and Azure Angel are all natural prominent racers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is no room for them all up front — realistically, American Affair, Jakajaro, Rumstar, and Spicy Marg are best-placed to press Asfoora into a fast but sustainable early gallop. The tactical verdict is clear: a strong, evenly-run pace with no genuine hold-up horses means prominent-to-pace racers who can travel into the race from just off the leader are most advantaged, while true closers are largely absent and the field will compress in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Asfoora Leads, Prompt Pressed
scenarios.trigger: If Asfoora breaks well and controls the pace under Murphy with American Affair and Jakajaro close behind, setting a fast but rhythmic gallop.
scenarios.body: Asfoora dictates from the front on her preferred Good to Firm Goodwood ground but faces a compressed field of prominent types who will keep her honest throughout; horses with the tactical speed to race in the first four without burning out win this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pouncers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace between Asfoora and her prominent rivals produces a strong early fractions that strings the field out, allowing a well-positioned stalker to pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Horses sitting second or third on the bridle can exploit tired leaders who burned energy disputing, and Goodwood's slight downhill gradient rewards those who switch off early and sprint late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly modest and the field bunches, allowing the redistributed midfield runners to close the gap with a late rush.
scenarios.body: This shape is structurally unlikely given the volume of genuine speed in the race, but if it does materialise, the handful of horses mapped to midfield who are actually prominent-natured could benefit from the cover and a strong finish; however, none are true hold-up closers, limiting their advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Night Raider Hold-Up Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to create a true end-to-end gallop that sees the front rank weaken sharply inside the final furlong, giving Night Raider a rare opportunity to close from the rear.
scenarios.body: Night Raider is the only genuine hold-up horse in this field with recent course-winning form at Goodwood over 5f and has won here fresh; this shape requires a genuinely gruelling pace that burns out the leaders, which is plausible but not the dominant probability.

watchPoints.text: Asfoora faces immediate pressure from American Affair, Jakajaro, Rumstar, and Spicy Marg — if she is harassed hard for the lead from the gates rather than allowed to stride clear, her winning chance diminishes sharply and the race opens up for a stalker.|

Lamborghini Bf drops from 6f to 5f for the first time at Goodwood on a track where the sprint chute suits confirmed speedsters — watch for signs of this Reuterskiold runner struggling to cope with the pace drop in the final furlong.|

Time For Sandals has never raced over 5f at Goodwood in five course appearances — her entire Goodwood profile is at 6f, and the extra furlong of pace required for this trip may expose a genuine stamina-in-reverse concern on quick ground.|

Night Raider is the only true hold-up horse in the race — if the leaders do not burn each other out sufficiently by the two-furlong pole, James Doyle will have nowhere near enough momentum from the rear to peg them back.|

The bulk of the redistributed runners — Jm Jungle, Aspect Island, Brussels, Dickensian, Argentine Tango — are all naturally prominent types who will be jostling for space in the first half of the field, creating potential for crowding, checking, and interference in the early stages of this 5f dash.|

races.paceDynamic: Jonquil is the confirmed front-runner here, and on Good To Firm ground at Goodwood over 1m1f, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable but honest gallop without any genuine rival attempting to match her stride for stride early. Boiling Point, Dividend, and Diego Ventura are all prominent types who will track up behind her, meaning the early order will be contested through the first two furlongs as those three jostle for the best positions just off the lead. The hold-up horses — Galen, Haatem, and Naqeeb — will settle in the rear quarter, needing Jonquil's pace to be genuine enough to string the field out and create room to finish through. This field holds more prominent and front-running types than the map can accommodate cleanly; Crown Of Oaks and Ambiente Friendly are true prominent and hold-up horses respectively who are unlikely to secure their preferred positions, with Boiling Point and Dividend best placed to occupy the prime tracking berths. The race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can travel smoothly just off the leader and produce a clean turn of foot on the Good To Firm surface — close-order stalkers are the profile to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jonquil Leads, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Jonquil sets an honest, uncontested gallop and the prominent trackers travel smoothly into the straight.
scenarios.body: Jonquil's honest pace strings the field out through the middle stages, leaving Boiling Point and Dividend perfectly positioned to pounce at the two-furlong pole without having to come from the clouds. Good To Firm Goodwood over 1m1f rewards horses who settle just off the pace and quicken efficiently, and this profile has the most runners capable of executing it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Find Gap
scenarios.trigger: If Jonquil's pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the field and the prominent horses are asked for effort earlier than ideal.
scenarios.body: A fast early tempo set by Jonquil burns off the prominent trackers, leaving Galen and Haatem — seasoned hold-up performers at Goodwood — to come through a tiring field in the final furlong. Both have strong course form at this trip and going, and their style suits a strongly-run race where the front rank has over-committed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Win
scenarios.trigger: If Jonquil is allowed to regulate a very modest gallop and nothing accelerates to challenge her until the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Without pressure, Jonquil slows the race into a sprint from two out, benefiting any horse good enough to match her acceleration from close range — Diego Ventura's win from a tracking position on this course becomes relevant here. Hold-up horses are left flat-footed as the race develops too quickly for them, and prominent types who settle without fighting for position reap the reward.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Crown Of Oaks and Ambiente Friendly causes a scrappy, uneven pace with surges mid-race.
scenarios.body: Crown Of Oaks, unable to secure a natural prominent spot, pushes up and disrupts the middle pack through the first half mile, creating an uneven tempo that scrambles the race shape unpredictably. This scenario hands an advantage to the most versatile jockey-horse combinations, with Colin Keane able to adapt Jonquil's role and Naqeeb's stamina coming into play at a distance where he has placed twice on this course.

watchPoints.text: Jonquil's true pace — if Colin Keane eases her back rather than fully front-running, the race loses its only pace anchor and the entire field will bunch dangerously entering the straight, scrambling all scenario probabilities.

Crown Of Oaks will be keen to stride forward from the gate; Tom Marquand must decide by the three-furlong marker whether to fight Boiling Point and Dividend for a tracking berth or drop back, and that choice directly affects which closers get a clear run.

Ambiente Friendly's headgear (p) is active and the horse ran in much longer-distance events recently — watch for him to be restless in running over a distance likely too sharp for his current conditioning.

races.paceDynamic: Jaijai is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push him from the gates, Pat Dobbs can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood — a track that naturally suits horses who can travel prominently and quicken on the descent. The prominent pack is exceptionally deep: Sky Secret, Revels, Clash Of Hearts, Dubai Champion, Innichen, and Sovereign Glory will all press forward aggressively behind Jaijai, ensuring the early sectionals are honest without becoming truly punishing, which historically at Goodwood over 6f rewards horses who sit just off the pace rather than those grinding from the rear. This field contains more prominent runners than the race shape can physically accommodate — Paper View, May Bee In Profit, Arabica Queen, and Global Success are all natural front-running or prominent types who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield against their instincts because the real estate ahead of them will already be taken by higher-rated rivals. The tactical verdict is clear: a well-judged, prominent-to-midfield position just behind Jaijai's controlled lead is the prime real estate here — horses who can sit third to sixth, travel smoothly on the Good to Firm turf, and produce a sustained finish from two furlongs out are most advantaged by this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jaijai Controls, Prominent Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Jaijai sets a measured pace and the prominent pack behind him race in their natural positions, producing a strongly-run final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Jaijai dictates from the front at a fair gallop, and the horses who have tracked him in positions three to six — particularly those with winning form over this trip at Goodwood on similar going — sweep past in a bunch finish that rewards tactical efficiency over raw stamina; the Good to Firm surface keeps the race sharp and favours quality over grinding speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack becomes compressed and multiple horses challenge Jaijai simultaneously from two furlongs out, creating a contested finish across the field.
scenarios.body: The sheer volume of prominent types forces an energetic final quarter-mile with several horses hitting the front together; horses with superior form at Goodwood over 6f and proven ability on Good to Firm carry the day in what becomes a test of class and finishing gears rather than positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is hotter than anticipated — driven by the crowded prominent group jostling for position — and the field strings out, leaving daylight for a closer.
scenarios.body: Persian Spring, who holds course form and has Jamie Spencer aboard for a patient delivery, could be delivered wide and late on the Good to Firm ground; Social Spirit and Wild Terrain could also benefit, though Wild Terrain's fade tendency makes the Persian Spring angle the more credible threat here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types — Paper View, May Bee In Profit, Arabica Queen — force their way forward and turn this into a truly contested sprint from the off, burning out the front-runners.
scenarios.body: A hot pace benefits the handful of genuine hold-up or midfield runners who can conserve energy and come with one clean run in the final furlong; however, because the true closers in this field are limited and several are racing below their natural form level, this remains the least likely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Jaijai's pace control is pivotal — if Pat Dobbs goes too slow in front the prominent pack will surge past him turning in, but if he pitches it right he controls the fractions for the whole field; watch his early position at the 4f marker to gauge whether this is a leader-wins or a leader-gets-caught race.

The volume of prominent-type runners — Sky Secret, Clash Of Hearts, Innichen, Revels, Dubai Champion among others — means the first two furlongs could be far quicker than a single front-runner scenario implies; any jostle or bump in the early stages could dramatically alter the race shape and compromise multiple fancied runners.

Paper View, May Bee In Profit, and Arabica Queen are all natural front-runners mapping into midfield under traffic pressure — if any of them force their way forward early it creates an additional pace pressure point that could turn a controlled race into a truly contested sprint, burning out Jaijai and several prominent horses simultaneously.

Wild Terrain's fade flag in the finish means David Probert must judge the delivery precisely — if this runner is produced too early from its hold-up position it will empty inside the final furlong, potentially causing interference as it tires across the wide Goodwood straight.

Persian Spring has gone 41 days between runs and is stepping up from 5f to 6f — if Jamie Spencer judges the hold-up delivery correctly on Good to Firm ground the extra furlong should suit, but watch whether Spencer goes wide for a clear run or attempts to thread through a packed field, as Goodwood's straight can be unforgiving for late challengers in big-field nurseries.

races.paceDynamic: Silver State is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse likely to lead, she should be able to dictate a controlled, even tempo over Goodwood's 1m3f on Good to Firm ground without being pressured into an unsustainable gallop. Pearl River, Pierian, Into The Light, Steel Raven and Leonardo Blu will all seek prominent positions just behind, creating a bunched chasing group rather than a contested lead — the pace is likely to be honest but not punishing. With Silver State able to regulate fractions from the front, the race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or in the first half of the field who can travel comfortably and pick off a tiring leader in the straight, rather than those requiring a strong pace to close into. The field carries more genuine prominent types than can all secure their natural berth — Silver State, Pearl River and Pierian are most likely to actually land front-running or close-up positions, while Magnatura, though a true prominent racer by nature, is mapped to midfield because the premium places near the pace are already oversubscribed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Track Off
scenarios.trigger: If Silver State dictates a measured pace and the front-running/prominent position proves decisive on the Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: Silver State sets a sustainable tempo and turns the race into a test of class and stamina at even fractions, suiting horses who travel prominently without burning fuel; the firm surface rewards those who race efficiently in the first half of the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Silver State is reeled in late by two prominent racers who track closely and quicken past her in the Goodwood straight.
scenarios.body: Pierian and Pearl River track the pace closely and use their superior class and recent winning form to sweep past Silver State in the final two furlongs; the Good to Firm ground amplifies the advantage of horses with a clean, prominent racing style and sound course form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finishers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptively quick and the prominent racers tie each other up, leaving ground for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Echo Of Stars or Devil's Peak, natural hold-up types with solid Goodwood form, make eye-catching late runs as the pace-pressers falter; this scenario requires the prominent pack to burn each other out sufficiently — plausible but against the likely controlled tempo Silver State will set.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early order breaks down with multiple prominent horses crowding each other and the race becomes positionally scrambled.
scenarios.body: A lower-rated horse finds an unexpected clear passage as the field shuffles, benefiting from gaps created by positional friction among the prominent group; Parisian Scholar, Astracornus or Mythical Valentine could be the unlikely beneficiary if true hold-up types manage to find the rail late.

watchPoints.text: Silver State's early fractions are critical — if Rose Dawes (5) allows her to bowl along unchallenged the leader could prove very hard to catch; watch the first two furlongs closely to judge whether the pace is truly sustainable or a false dawdle.

Parisian Scholar ran just 2 days ago — monitor his market moves and paddock demeanour closely, as a quick turnaround at this level is unusual and could mean he is not at his sharpest, or conversely that connections are supremely confident.

Leonardo Blu makes an aggressive trip extension from 8f to 1m3f in one jump — if he fails to settle prominently in the early stages with five rivals fighting for the same ground, he risks being caught in a pocket and running out of race.

Magnatura and Mythical Valentine are both competing for positions that their natural racing styles demand but the field shape will deny them — watch whether either jockey makes an early decision to either force the issue or drop out, as both outcomes materially alter the race shape.

Kenergy's debut on turf and debut at Goodwood simultaneously makes her a genuine unknown quantity — if she breaks sharply and shows unexpected natural pace, she could unsettle the order behind Silver State and compress the chasing pack earlier than expected.

runners_data.note: William Haggas's 3yo is the only confirmed front-runner and opened her account over 10f at Goodwood last time; Saffie Osborne keeps the ride, she has a tongue-tie, and carrying just 118lbs gives a light weight pull — uncontested front-running on Good to Firm at this track is a material advantage.
runners_data.comment: Silver Lake won last time out to arrive here in form, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — but ranked last on our figures, there is a significant gap to bridge against this field.

races.paceDynamic: Silver Lake is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one rival naturally ahead of the field, she should stride into an uncontested lead and set a measured, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Goodwood. Lady Dora Mae and Folk Pageant are the principal prominent challengers who will look to track closely, while Spinning Lizzie is another who wants to race handily — this creates a competitive quartet for the front positions. Zgharta and Room Fourteen are genuine prominent-types by nature but are redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more front-runners and prominent horses than the race shape can accommodate; Silver Lake and Lady Dora Mae are most likely to actually secure the positions they want, with Folk Pageant and Spinning Lizzie also pressing for cover just off the pace. With the gallop likely to be honest but not brutal, and the emphasis on horses travelling smoothly in mid-to-close range before producing a sustained finish on fast ground, this race shape most favours prominent racers with proven Goodwood form who can handle a true-run test from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Silver Lake Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Lake bowls along in front without meaningful pressure and the pace is even but not searingly fast.
scenarios.body: Silver Lake controls tempo from the outset, finds her rivals unable to dominate early and simply extends her advantage from the home turn on good-to-firm ground she handles well; the form-fit for a Haggas-trained 3yo with recent Goodwood winning form is compelling at a generous weight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent runners — Lady Dora Mae, Folk Pageant or Spinning Lizzie — apply sustained pressure that leaves Silver Lake vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop set by Silver Lake invites a close-tracking rival to pick up past her as she ties late; Lady Dora Mae's Goodwood course-and-distance placing and Spinning Lizzie's sharp form suit a race where they can sit a length or two off the pace and pounce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Swoops Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and a hold-up horse gets a clear run through a tiring pack.
scenarios.body: Wisper is the only genuine hold-up runner in the field and has recent course-and-distance form that includes a Goodwood win at this trip; she requires the front contingent to push the pace beyond comfort, which is unlikely with a single front-runner, but not impossible given the prominent horses pressing Silver Lake.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Produces Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Lake is pressed hard early by multiple prominent rivals and the race turns ragged with a slow final-furlong scramble.
scenarios.body: An unsettled gallop could see Folk Pageant, whose trainer has lower recent strike rate but whose form over 10f on Good ground is solid, stay on powerfully; this scenario suits horses with strong finishing kicks over the extended trip rather than pure front-running types.

watchPoints.text: Silver Lake (Haggas/Osborne) goes unchallenged to the front — if no rival tests her before the home turn, watch whether she simply extends clear as she did at this course last time.

Room Fourteen is equipped with headgear (h) and Ryan Moore will attempt to get her closer to the pace than the map suggests; if he manoeuvres her into a prominent position, her Goodwood course record makes her dangerous.

Zgharta with Oisin Murphy is the redistribution risk — Murphy may use his tactical intelligence to force a prominent berth against the pace map; if he succeeds, Andrew Balding's filly's form here looks live.

Wisper's chances are almost entirely contingent on a contested, pressured gallop — watch how hard Lady Dora Mae and Spinning Lizzie chase Silver Lake in the first half mile to determine whether the hold-up play is even viable.
